quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you know about the oily strip down the center of a lane?

options.text: You should only ride on it if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
It usually gives good traction for riding, but not when it is raining.
You should always avoid it.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually gives good traction for riding, but not when it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip of the road is usually oily but gives good traction for riding, except when it is raining. The oily strip is usually less than two feet wide. Motorcyclists can ride on either side of the strip and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Which choice is NOT a way to control your motorcycle in a turn?

options.text: Speed up through the turn.
Slow down before turning.
Lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up through the turn.
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle in a turn, slow down before you enter the turn. Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Press the handlebar to lean in the right direction. Then gently speed up as you go through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up quickly as it gets close.
Swerve around the dog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up quickly as it gets close.
questions.explanation: If you see a dog approaching, slow down and downshift until you are close to it. Then quickly speed up and move away from the dog as it approaches.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to use your headlight on high beam during the day and night, whenever it is legal and safe. Use your running lights too if you have them.

questions.question: What does it feel like if your front tire goes flat?

options.text: The steering feels heavy.
The steering feels loose.
The steering feels soft.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering feels heavy.
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycle brakes is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
The front and rear brakes are equally powerful.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake of a motorcycle is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your total stopping power.

questions.question: When you ride behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
The driver usually cannot see you.
You should avoid this position.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride in a position so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Ride in the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors, so this position makes it more likely they will see you.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
Stop at the stop sign and then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and use your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the part of the lane where other drivers can see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, who must yield?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
You should go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, if you and another driver arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When riding with a group of motorcyclists, when should you NOT use a staggered formation?

options.text: You should always use it.
You should not use it when entering or exiting a highway.
You should not use it when riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should not use it when entering or exiting a highway.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually good, but switch to single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the motorcyclist's following distance should:

options.text: Increase.
Decrease.
Stay the same as normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: A motorcyclist towing a trailer should increase their following distance. The trailer adds weight, so the motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: An engine will seize due to:

options.text: A lack of oil.
A lack of fuel.
Improper tire inflation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lack of oil.
questions.explanation: Engines seize when they are low on oil. Without oil, the engine's moving parts overheat and cannot move smoothly.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
Release the front brake right away and use only the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake immediately and re-apply it.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Ride carefully when approaching an intersection. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes to reduce your reaction time if needed.

questions.question: Service signs are:

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders can cause you to steer off course.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front so you can see farther down the road.
Keep riding at your normal speed to avoid being hit from behind.
Slow down and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase your following distance. You can see less at night, so you need more time and space to react to hazards.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the far side of your lane away from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
Has no impact on safety either way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: When being passed, do not move to the far side of your lane. This may encourage the passing driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, which brake provides the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go ahead slowly.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, come to a complete stop. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: In broad daylight.
At dusk.
At night.

questions.correctAnswerText: In broad daylight.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials when you ride, even during daylight.

questions.question: While riding, you should:

options.text: Always look in the rearview mirror.
Check the rearview mirror often.
Never use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirror often as part of your normal riding routine. Use your mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: The best lane position for a motorcycle:

options.text: Is on the left side of the lane, near the centerline.
Is on the right side of the lane, near the curb.
Changes based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position works best in all situations. Choose the position that gives you the best view and the most space around you. Move to different positions as traffic changes.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be used during daylight.
Be used without a driver license.
Be used with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.
